title: The scheme theoretic image of a quasi-compact morphism after an admissible blowup is the strict transform of the original image
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For morphisms X -> S and Y -> S, an open U of X, a quasi-compact morphism V -> X x_S Y whose composite with the first projection lands in U, and the scheme theoretic image Z of V, the lemma states that for any U-admissible blowup X' -> X the scheme theoretic image of V -> X' x_S Y is the strict transform of Z (statement lines 9727-9737). The proof identifies the strict transform Z' with a closed subscheme of X' x_S Y, so that it suffices to show the scheme theoretic image Z'' of V -> Z' equals Z' (proof lines 9740-9745). Then it uses quasi-compactness, which passes to the base change because X' x_S Y -> X x_S Y is separated as a base change of a proper morphism, to conclude that Z'' and Z agree away from the exceptional divisor, and finishes by observing that the surjection O_{Z'} -> O_{Z''} must be an isomorphism because the structure sheaf of a strict transform has no nonzero sections supported on the exceptional divisor (proof lines 9746-9758). Replacing a comparison of images by an isomorphism criterion for a surjection of structure sheaves with no sections supported on the exceptional divisor is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
